≲max⁡{(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)(1−b)/a,M1−b}\displaystyle\lesssim\max\big\{(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{(1-b)/a},\ M^{1-b}\big\}

when b<a+1b<a+1, where in the last inequality, we choose k2=[M/3]∧(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)1/ak_{2}=[M/3]\wedge(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{1/a} to minimize the upper bound.

When (N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)1/a≤M/c(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{1/{a}}\leq M/c for some large constant c>0c>0, combining Lemma D.2 and G.4 yields the lower bound

𝔼𝐰∗​𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌​(𝐰∗)\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{{\mathbf{w}^{*}}}\mathsf{Bias}(\mathbf{w}^{*}) ≳∑i:λ~i<1/(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)μi​(𝐒𝐇𝐇𝐰​𝐇𝐒⊤)μi​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)≂∑i:λ~i<1/(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)μi​(𝐒𝐇(a+b)/a​𝐒⊤)μi​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤),\displaystyle\gtrsim\sum_{i:\tilde{\lambda}_{i}<1/(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)}\frac{\mu_{i}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{H}^{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})}{\mu_{i}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})}\eqsim\sum_{i:\tilde{\lambda}_{i}<1/(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)}\frac{\mu_{i}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}^{(a+b)/a}\mathbf{S}^{\top})}{\mu_{i}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})},
≳∑λ~i<1/(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ),i≤Mi−(a+b)i−a=∑λi<1/(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ),i≤Mi−b≳(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)(1−b)/a\displaystyle\gtrsim\sum_{\tilde{\lambda}_{i}<1/(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma),i\leq M}\frac{i^{-(a+b)}}{i^{-a}}=\sum_{\lambda_{i}<1/(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma),i\leq M}i^{-b}\gtrsim(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{(1-b)/{a}}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Here, the hidden constants depend only on a,b.a,b.

Upper bound when b≥a+1b\geq a+1.

Following the previous derivations, when b=a+1b=a+1, we have with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}

𝔼𝐰∗​𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌​(𝐰∗)\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\mathsf{Bias}(\mathbf{w}^{*}) ≲𝔼𝐰∗[∥𝐰∗0:k2∥22N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ+∥𝐰k2:∞∗∥𝐇k2:∞2]\displaystyle\lesssim{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\Bigg[\frac{\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{0:k_{2}}}}\|_{2}^{2}}{N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma}+\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\|^{2}_{\mathbf{H}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\Bigg]

where the last line follows by setting k2=[M/3]∧(N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)1/ak_{2}=[M/3]\wedge(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{1/a}. When b>a+1b>a+1, we have with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}

𝔼𝐰∗​𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌​(𝐰∗)\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\mathsf{Bias}(\mathbf{w}^{*}) ≲𝔼𝐰∗[∥𝐰∗0:k2∥22N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ+∥𝐰k2:∞∗∥𝐇k2:∞2]\displaystyle\lesssim{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\Bigg[\frac{\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{0:k_{2}}}}\|_{2}^{2}}{N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma}+\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\|^{2}_{\mathbf{H}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\Bigg]

≲1N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ+M1−b,\displaystyle\lesssim\frac{1}{N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma}+M^{1-b},

where the last follows by chooing k2=M/3k_{2}=M/3 to minimize the upper bound.

Note that there exist non-constant gaps between the upper and lower bounds on the bias term (plus the approximation error term, Lemma C.5) in the simple regime where b≥a+1b\geq a+1. We leave a more precise analysis of the bias term for future work.

Lemma D.5 (Bounds on 𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌\mathsf{Bias} under the logarithmic power-law spectrum).

Suppose Assumption 4 hold and the initial stepsize γ≤1c​tr⁡(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)\gamma\leq\frac{1}{c\tr(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})} for some constant c>2c>2. and

when (N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)≤Mc(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)\leq M^{c} for some sufficiently small constant c>0c>0. Here, all constants depend only on the power-law degree a.a.

Proof of Lemma D.5.

For the upper bound, using Lemma G.7, D.1 and the assumption that 𝔼​𝐰i∗2=1{\mathbb{E}}{\mathbf{w}^{*2}_{i}}=1 for all i>0i>0, with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}, we have

𝔼𝐰∗​𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌​(𝐰∗)\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\mathsf{Bias}(\mathbf{w}^{*}) ≲𝔼𝐰∗[∥𝐰∗0:k2∥22N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ+∥𝐰k2:∞∗∥𝐇k2:∞2]\displaystyle\lesssim{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\Bigg[\frac{\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{0:k_{2}}}}\|_{2}^{2}}{N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma}+\|{\mathbf{w}^{*}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\|^{2}_{\mathbf{H}_{{k_{2}:\infty}}}\Bigg]

Appendix E Variance error

In this section, we present matching upper and lower bounds on the variance term 𝖵𝖺𝗋\mathsf{Var} defined in (6) under the power-law or logarithmic power-law spectrum.

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} over the randomness of 𝐒\mathbf{S}. Here the hidden constants may depend on a.a. ∎

Appendix F Expected risk of the average of (SGD) iterates

In this section, we study the expected risk of the average of (SGD) iterates. Namely, we consider a fixed stepsize  (SGD) procedure where γt=γ\gamma_{t}=\gamma and define 𝐯¯N:=∑i=0N−1𝐯i/N\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{N}:=\sum^{N-1}_{i=0}\mathbf{v}_{i}/N. Our goal is to derive matching upper and lower bounds ℛ⁡(𝐯¯N)\mathcal{R}(\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{N}) in terms of the sample size NN and model size M.M. Compared with the last iterate of (SGD) with geometrically decaying stepsizes, we show that the average of (SGD) iterates with a fixed stepsize achieves a better risk, in the sense that the effective sample size N𝚎𝚏𝚏N_{\mathtt{eff}} is replaced by NN in the bounds (c.f. Theorem 4.1). This may give improvement up to logarithmic factors.

We start with invoking the following result in Zou et al. (2023).

𝔼​ℛM​(𝐯¯N)−σ2≂𝔼𝐰∗​𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗑+𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌+σ2​𝖵𝖺𝗋,\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\mathcal{R}_{M}({\mathbf{\bar{v}}}_{N})-\sigma^{2}\eqsim{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}\mathsf{Approx}+\mathsf{Bias}+\sigma^{2}\mathsf{Var},

where the expectation of ℛM\mathcal{R}_{M} is over 𝐰∗\mathbf{w}^{*} and (𝐱i,yi)i=1N(\mathbf{x}_{i},y_{i})_{i=1}^{N} and

With these results at hand, we are ready to derive upper and lower bounds for the risk of the average of (SGD) iterates.

F.1 Matching bounds for the average of (SGD) iterates under power-law spectrum

In this section, we derive upper and lower bounds for the expected risk under the power-law spectrum. Our main result (Theorem F.6) follows directly from Theorem F.1 and the bounds on Ti​(i=1,2,3,4){T}_{i}(i=1,2,3,4) in Lemmas F.2, F.3, F.4 and F.5.

Theorem F.6 (Scaling law for average iterates of SGD).

Suppose Assumption 1 and 2 hold and σ2≲1\sigma^{2}\lesssim 1. Then there exists some aa-dependent constant c>0c>0 such that when γ≤c\gamma\leq c, with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} over the randomness of the sketch matrix 𝐒\mathbf{S}, we have

𝔼​ℛM​(𝐯¯N)=σ2+Θ⁡(M1−a)+Θ⁡((N​γ)1/a−1),\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\mathcal{R}_{M}(\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{N})=\sigma^{2}+\Theta\big(M^{1-a}\big)+\Theta\big((N\gamma)^{1/a-1}\big),

where the expectation is over the randomness of 𝐰∗\mathbf{w}^{*} and (𝐱i,yi)i=1N(\mathbf{x}_{i},y_{i})_{i=1}^{N}, and Θ⁡(⋅)\Theta(\cdot) hides constants that may depend on aa.

See the proof in Section F.2.6.

Compared with Theorem 4.1, Theorem F.6 suggests that the average of  (SGD) achieves a smaller risk in the sketched linear model—the (N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ)1/a(N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma)^{1/a} is replaced by (N​γ)1/a(N\gamma)^{1/a} in the bound for the bias term. This is intuitive since the sum of stepsizes ∑tγt≂N𝚎𝚏𝚏​γ\sum_{t}\gamma_{t}\eqsim N_{\mathtt{eff}}\gamma for the geometrically decaying stepsize scheduler while ∑tγt≂N​γ\sum_{t}\gamma_{t}\eqsim N\gamma for the fixed stepsize scheduler.

We also verify the observations in Theorem F.6 via simulations. We adopt the same model and setup as in Section 5 but use the average of iterates of fixed stepsize  (SGD) (denoted by 𝐯¯N\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{N}) as the predictor. From Figure 3 and 4 we see that the expected risk 𝔼​ℛ​(𝐯¯N){\mathbb{E}}\mathcal{R}(\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{N}) also scales following a power-law relation in both sample size NN and model size MM. Moreover, the fitted exponents match our theoretical predictions in Theorem F.6.

F.2 Proofs

F.2.1 Proof of Theorem F.1

Similar to the proof of Theorem A.4, we have the decomposition

ℛ⁡(𝐯¯N)\displaystyle\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{\bar{v}}}_{N}) =σ2+𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗑+‖𝐯¯N−𝐯∗‖𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤2.\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}+\mathsf{Approx}+\|{\mathbf{\bar{v}}}_{N}-{\mathbf{v}^{*}}\|_{\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top}}^{2}.

Note that (𝐯t)t=1N(\mathbf{v}_{t})_{t=1}^{N} can also be viewed as the SGD iterates on the model y=⟨𝐒𝐱,𝐯∗⟩+ξ+ϵy=\langle\mathbf{S}\mathbf{x},{\mathbf{v}^{*}}\rangle+\xi+\epsilon, where the noise satisfies

𝔼​(ξ+ϵ)2=ℛ⁡(𝐯∗)=𝔼​ξ2+σ2.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}(\xi+\epsilon)^{2}=\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{v}^{*}})=\mathbb{E}\xi^{2}+\sigma^{2}.

Therefore, the upper and lower bounds on 𝖡𝗂𝖺𝗌,𝖵𝖺𝗋\mathsf{Bias},\mathsf{Var} follow directly from the proof of Theorem 2.1, 2.2 and related lemmas (Lemma B.6, B.11, C.3, C.5) in Zou et al. (2023).

F.2.2 Proof of Lemma F.2

T4≲‖𝐰∗‖𝐇2⋅Deff,NN.\displaystyle{T}_{4}\lesssim\|\mathbf{w}_{*}\|_{\mathbf{H}}^{2}\cdot\frac{{D_{\mathrm{eff},N}}}{N}.

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

Appendix G Concentration lemmas

G.1 General concentration results

Lemma G.1.

Suppose that 𝐒∈ℝM×d\mathbf{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times d} is such that 33 3 We allow d=∞d=\infty.

𝐒i​j∼𝒩⁡(0,1/M).\mathbf{S}_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1/M).

Let (λi)i≥1(\lambda_{i})_{i\geq 1} be the eigenvalues of 𝐇\mathbf{H} in non-increasing order. Let (λ~i)i=1M(\tilde{\lambda}_{i})_{i=1}^{M} be the eigenvalues of 𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top} in non-increasing order. Then there exists a constant c>1c>1 such that for every M≥0M\geq 0 and every 0≤k≤M0\leq k\leq M, with probability ≥1−e−Ω⁡(M)−e−Ω⁡(k)\geq 1-e^{-\Omega(M)}-e^{-\Omega(k)}, we have

for every​j≤M,|λ~j−(λj+∑i>kλiM)|≤c⋅(kM⋅λj+λk+1+∑i>kλi2M).\displaystyle\text{for every}\ j\leq M,\quad\bigg|\tilde{\lambda}_{j}-\bigg(\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\bigg)\bigg|\leq c\cdot\Bigg(\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}+\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg).

As a direct consequence, for k≤M/c2k\leq M/c^{2}, we have

for every​j≤M,|λ~j−(λj+∑i>kλiM)|≤12⋅(λj+∑i>kλiM)+c1⋅λk+1,\displaystyle\text{for every}\ j\leq M,\quad\bigg|\tilde{\lambda}_{j}-\bigg(\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\bigg)\bigg|\leq\frac{1}{2}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\bigg)+c_{1}\cdot\lambda_{k+1},

where c1=c+2​c2c_{1}=c+2c^{2}.

Proof of Lemma G.1.

We have the following decomposition motivated by Swartworth and Woodruff (2023) (see their Section 3.4, Proof of Theorem 1).

𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤\displaystyle\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top} =𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤+𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤\displaystyle=\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}+\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}
=𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M+𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M.\displaystyle=\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}+\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}.

We remark that this decomposition idea has been implicitly used in Bartlett et al. (2020) to control the eigenvalues of a Gram matrix. In fact, we will use techniques from Bartlett et al. (2020) to obtain a sharper bound than that presented in Swartworth and Woodruff (2023).

For the upper bound, we have

μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top}\big) ≤μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M)+∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥2\displaystyle\leq\mu_{j}\bigg(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg)+\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|_{2}
=μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M+∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥2\displaystyle=\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}+\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|_{2}
≤μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M+c1⋅(λk+1+∑i>kλi2M),\displaystyle\leq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}+c_{1}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg),

where the last inequality is by Lemma G.2. For j≤kj\leq k, using Lemma G.3, we have

μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)≤λj+c2⋅kM⋅λj.\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)\leq\lambda_{j}+c_{2}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}.

For k<j≤Mk<j\leq M, we have

μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)=0≤λj+c2⋅kM⋅λj.\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)=0\leq\lambda_{j}+c_{2}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}.

Putting these together, we have the following for every j=1,…,Mj=1,\dots,M:

μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top}\big) ≤μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M+c1⋅(λk+1+∑i>kλi2M)\displaystyle\leq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}+c_{1}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg)
≤λj+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M+c⋅(kM⋅λj+λk+1+∑i>kλi2M).\displaystyle\leq\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}+c\cdot\Bigg(\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}+\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg).

Similarly, we can show the lower bound. By the decomposition, we have

μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top}\big) ≥μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M)−∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥\displaystyle\geq\mu_{j}\bigg(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg)-\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|
=μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M−∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥\displaystyle=\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}-\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|
≥μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M−c1⋅(λk+1+∑i>kλi2M),\displaystyle\geq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}-c_{1}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg),

where the last inequality is by Lemma G.2. For j≤kj\leq k, using Lemma G.3, we have

μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)≥λj−c2⋅kM⋅λj.\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)\geq\lambda_{j}-c_{2}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}.

For k<j≤Mk<j\leq M, we have

μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)=0≥λj−λk+1−c2⋅kM⋅λj,\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)=0\geq\lambda_{j}-\lambda_{k+1}-c_{2}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j},

where the last inequality is due to λj≤λk\lambda_{j}\leq\lambda_{k} for j≥kj\geq k. Putting these together, we have

μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top}\big) ≥μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M−c1⋅(λk+1+∑i>kλi2M)\displaystyle\geq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\big)+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}-c_{1}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg)
≥λj+∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M−c⋅(kM⋅λj+λk+1+∑i>kλi2M).\displaystyle\geq\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}-c\cdot\Bigg(\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}+\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}\Bigg).

So far, we have proved the first claim. To show the second claim, we simply apply

c⋅kM≤12for​k≤M/c2,c\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\leq\frac{1}{2}\quad\text{for}\ k\leq M/c^{2},

and

c⋅∑i>kλi2M\displaystyle c\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}} ≤c⋅∑i>kλiM⋅λk+1\displaystyle\leq c\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\lambda_{k+1}}
≤12⋅∑i>kλiM+2​c2⋅λk+1,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}+2c^{2}\cdot\lambda_{k+1},

in the first claim. ∎

Lemma G.2 (Tail concentration, Lemma 26 in Bartlett et al. (2020)).

For any k≥0k\geq 0, with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}, we have

∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥2≲λk+1+∑i>kλi2M.\displaystyle\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|_{2}\lesssim\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}}.

Moreover, the minimum eigenvalue of 𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top} satisfies

μmin(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)≳λk+2​M\displaystyle{\mu_{\min}}(\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top})\gtrsim\lambda_{k+2M}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

Proof of Lemma G.2.

The first part of Lemma G.2 is a version of Lemma 26 in (Bartlett et al., 2020) (see their proof). We provide proof here for completeness.

We write 𝐒∈ℝM×p\mathbf{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times p} as

𝐒=(𝐬1…𝐬p),𝐬i∼𝒩⁡(0,1M⋅𝐈M),i≥1.\mathbf{S}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{s}_{1}&\ldots&\mathbf{s}_{p}\end{pmatrix},\quad\mathbf{s}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(0,\ \frac{1}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg),\quad i\geq 1.

Since Gaussian distribution is rotational invariance, without loss of generality, we may assume

𝐇=diag⁡{λ1,…,λp}.\mathbf{H}=\diag\{\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{p}\}.

Then we have

𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤=∑i>kλi𝐬i𝐬i⊤.\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}=\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}\mathbf{s}_{i}\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}.

Fixing a unit vector 𝐯∈ℝM\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{M}, then

𝐯⊤𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤𝐯=∑i>kλi(𝐬i⊤𝐯)2,\mathbf{v}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}\mathbf{v}=\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}\big(\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v}\big)^{2},

where each 𝐬i⊤​𝐯\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v} is (1/M)(1/M)-subGaussian. By Bernstein’s inequality, we have, with probability ≥1−δ\geq 1-\delta,

|∑i>kλi​(𝐬i⊤​𝐯)2−∑i>kλiM|≲1M⋅(λk+1⋅log⁡1δ+∑i>kλi2⋅log⁡1δ).\displaystyle\bigg|\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}\big(\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v}\big)^{2}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\bigg|\lesssim\frac{1}{M}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{k+1}\cdot\log\frac{1}{\delta}+\sqrt{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}\cdot\log\frac{1}{\delta}}\bigg).

By a union bound and net argument on 𝒮M−1\mathcal{S}^{M-1}, we have, with probability ≥1−δ\geq 1-\delta, for every unit vector 𝐯∈ℝM\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{M},

|∑i>kλi​(𝐬i⊤​𝐯)2−∑i>kλiM|≲1M⋅(λk+1⋅(M+log⁡1δ)+∑i>kλi2⋅(M+log⁡1δ)).\displaystyle\bigg|\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}\big(\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v}\big)^{2}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\bigg|\lesssim\frac{1}{M}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}\cdot\bigg(M+\log\frac{1}{\delta}\bigg)+\sqrt{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}\cdot\bigg(M+\log\frac{1}{\delta}\bigg)}\Bigg).

So with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}, we have

∥𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤−∑i>kλiM⋅𝐈M∥2\displaystyle\bigg\|\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}-\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}\bigg\|_{2} ≲1M⋅(λk+1⋅M+∑i>kλi2⋅M)\displaystyle\lesssim\frac{1}{M}\cdot\Bigg(\lambda_{k+1}\cdot M+\sqrt{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}\cdot M}\Bigg)
≂λk+1+∑i>kλi2M,\displaystyle\eqsim\lambda_{k+1}+\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}^{2}}{M}},

which completes the proof of the first part of Lemma G.2.

To prove the second part of Lemma G.2, it suffices to note that

𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤⪰∑i=k+12​M+kλi𝐬i𝐬i⊤⪰λ2​M+k⋅∑i=k+12​M+k𝐬i𝐬i⊤⪰cλ2​M+k⋅𝐈M\displaystyle\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top}\succeq\sum_{i=k+1}^{2M+k}\lambda_{i}\mathbf{s}_{i}\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\succeq\lambda_{2M+k}\cdot\sum_{i=k+1}^{2M+k}\mathbf{s}_{i}\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\succeq c\lambda_{2M+k}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{M}

for some constant c>1c>1 with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}, where the last line follows from concentration properties of Gaussian covariance matrices (see e.g., Thereom 6.1 Wainwright (2019)). ∎

Lemma G.3 (Head concentration).

With probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)−e−Ω⁡(k)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}-e^{-\Omega(k)}, we have

for everyj≤k,|μj(𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤)−λj|≲kM⋅λj.\displaystyle\text{for every}\ j\leq k,\quad|\mu_{j}(\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top})-\lambda_{j}|\lesssim\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}.
Proof of Lemma G.3.

Note that the spectrum of 𝐒0:k𝐇0:k𝐒0:k⊤\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top} is indentical to the spectrum of 𝐇1/20:k𝐒0:k⊤𝐒0:k𝐇1/20:k\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}. We will bound the latter. We start with bounding the spectrum of 𝐒0:k𝐒0:k⊤\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}. To this end, we write 𝐒0:k⊤∈ℝk×M\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times M} as

𝐒0:k⊤=(𝐬1…𝐬M),𝐬i∼𝒩(0,1M⋅𝐈k),i=1,…,M.\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{0:k}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{s}_{1}&\ldots&\mathbf{s}_{M}\end{pmatrix},\quad\mathbf{s}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(0,\ \frac{1}{M}\cdot\mathbf{I}_{k}\bigg),\quad i=1,\dots,M.

Then repeating the argument in Lemma G.2, we have, with probability ≥1−δ\geq 1-\delta, for every unit vector 𝐯∈ℝk\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{k},

|𝐯⊤𝐒0:k⊤𝐒0:k𝐯−1|\displaystyle\big|\mathbf{v}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{v}-1\big| =|∑i=1M(𝐬i⊤​𝐯)2−1|\displaystyle=\bigg|\sum_{i=1}^{M}\big(\mathbf{s}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v}\big)^{2}-1\bigg|
≲1M⋅(1⋅(k+log⁡1δ)+M⋅(k+log⁡1δ))\displaystyle\lesssim\frac{1}{M}\cdot\Bigg(1\cdot\bigg(k+\log\frac{1}{\delta}\bigg)+\sqrt{M\cdot\bigg(k+\log\frac{1}{\delta}\bigg)}\Bigg)
≲k+log⁡(1/δ)M.\displaystyle\lesssim\sqrt{\frac{k+\log(1/\delta)}{M}}.

So we have, with probability ≥1−e−Ω⁡(k)\geq 1-e^{-\Omega(k)},

∥𝐒0:k⊤𝐒0:k−𝐈k∥2≲kM.\displaystyle\big\|\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}-\mathbf{I}_{k}\big\|_{2}\lesssim\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}.

This implies that

μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐒0:k⊤𝐒0:k𝐇0:k1/2)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}\big) ≤μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐇0:k1/2)+c1⋅kM⋅μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐇0:k1/2)\displaystyle\leq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\big)+c_{1}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\big)
=λj+c1⋅kM⋅λj,\displaystyle=\lambda_{j}+c_{1}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j},

and that

μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐒0:k⊤𝐒0:k𝐇0:k1/2)\displaystyle\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}^{\top}\mathbf{S}_{0:k}\mathbf{H}^{1/2}_{0:k}\big) ≥μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐇0:k1/2)−c1⋅kM⋅μj(𝐇0:k1/2𝐇0:k1/2)\displaystyle\geq\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\big)-c_{1}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\mu_{j}\big(\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\mathbf{H}_{0:k}^{1/2}\big)
=λj−c1⋅kM⋅λj.\displaystyle=\lambda_{j}-c_{1}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}\cdot\lambda_{j}.

We have completed the proof. ∎

G.2 Concentration results under power-law spectrum

Lemma G.4 (Eigenvalues of 𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top} under power-law spectrum).

Suppose Assumption 2 hold. There exist aa-dependent constants c2>c1>0c_{2}>c_{1}>0 such that

c1​j−a≤μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)≤c2​j−a\displaystyle c_{1}j^{-{a}}\leq\mu_{j}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})\leq c_{2}j^{-{a}}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M).1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

Proof of Lemma G.4.

Let (λ~i)i=1M(\tilde{\lambda}_{i})_{i=1}^{M} denote the eigenvalues of 𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top} in non-increasing order. Using Lemma G.1 with k=M/ck=M/c for some sufficiently large constant cc and noting that ∑i>ki−a≂k1−a\sum_{i>k}i^{-{a}}\eqsim k^{1-{a}}, we have

12⋅(j−a+c~1​M−a)−c~2⋅M−a≤λ~j≤32⋅(j−a+c~1​M−a)+c~2⋅M−a\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\cdot(j^{-{a}}+\tilde{c}_{1}M^{-{a}})-\tilde{c}_{2}\cdot M^{-{a}}\leq\tilde{\lambda}_{j}\leq\frac{3}{2}\cdot(j^{-{a}}+\tilde{c}_{1}M^{-{a}})+\tilde{c}_{2}\cdot M^{-{a}}

for every j∈[M]j\in[M] for some constants c~i,i∈[2]\tilde{c}_{i},i\in[2] with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Therefore, for all j≤M/c~j\leq M/\tilde{c} for some sufficiently large constant c~>1\tilde{c}>1, we have

λ~j∈[c~3​j−a,c~4​j−a]\displaystyle\tilde{\lambda}_{j}\in[\tilde{c}_{3}j^{-{a}},\tilde{c}_{4}j^{-{a}}]

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constants c~3,c~4>0\tilde{c}_{3},\tilde{c}_{4}>0. For j∈[M/c~,M]j\in[M/\tilde{c},M], by monotonicity of the eigenvalues, we have

λ~j≤λ~⌊M/c~⌋≤c~4​(⌊Mc~⌋)−a≤c~5​M−a≤c~5​j−a\displaystyle\tilde{\lambda}_{j}\leq\tilde{\lambda}_{\lfloor M/\tilde{c}\rfloor}\leq\tilde{c}_{4}\Big(\Big\lfloor\frac{M}{\tilde{c}}\Big\rfloor\Big)^{-{a}}\leq\tilde{c}_{5}M^{-{a}}\leq\tilde{c}_{5}j^{-{a}}

for some sufficiently large constant c~5>c~4\tilde{c}_{5}>\tilde{c}_{4} with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Moreover, using Lemma G.2 with k=0k=0, we obtain

λ~j≥λ~M≥μmin(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)≥c~6λ~2​M≥c~7(M/c~)−a≥c~8j−a\displaystyle\tilde{\lambda}_{j}\geq\tilde{\lambda}_{M}\geq{\mu_{\min}}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top})\geq\tilde{c}_{6}\tilde{\lambda}_{2M}\geq\tilde{c}_{7}(M/\tilde{c})^{-{a}}\geq\tilde{c}_{8}j^{-{a}}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constants c~6,c~7,c~8>0\tilde{c}_{6},\tilde{c}_{7},\tilde{c}_{8}>0. Combining the bounds for j≤M/c~j\leq M/\tilde{c} and j∈[M/c~,M]j\in[M/\tilde{c},M] completes the proof. ∎

Lemma G.5 (Ratio of eigenvalues of 𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top} under power-law spectrum).

Suppose Assumption 2 hold. There exists some aa-dependent constant c>0c>0 such that for any k≥1k\geq 1, the ratio between the M/2M/2-th and MM-th eigenvalues

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)≤c\displaystyle\frac{\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}{\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}\leq c

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M).1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

Proof of Lemma G.5.

Let c>0c>0 be some sufficiently large constant. Applying Lemma G.1 with 𝐇k:∞\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty} replacing 𝐇\mathbf{H}, for k0=M/ck_{0}=M/c, we have

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≤32⋅(λM/2+k+∑i>k0λi+kM)+c1⋅λk0+1+k,\displaystyle\leq\frac{3}{2}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{M/2+k}+\frac{\sum_{i>k_{0}}\lambda_{i+k}}{M}\bigg)+c_{1}\cdot\lambda_{k_{0}+1+k},
≲(M2+k)−a+(k0+k)1−aM+(k0+1+k)−a\displaystyle\lesssim\big(\frac{M}{2}+k\big)^{-{a}}+\frac{(k_{0}+k)^{1-{a}}}{M}+(k_{0}+1+k)^{-{a}}
≲(k∨M)−a+(k∨M)−a​(1∨kM)+(k∨M)−a\displaystyle\lesssim(k\vee M)^{-{a}}+(k\vee M)^{-{a}}\big(1\vee\frac{k}{M}\big)+(k\vee M)^{-{a}}
≲(k∨M)−a​(1∨kM)\displaystyle\lesssim(k\vee M)^{-{a}}\big(1\vee\frac{k}{M}\big) (35)

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constant c1>0c_{1}>0.

Case 11: k≲Mk\lesssim M

From Lemma G.2, we have

μmin(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle{\mu_{\min}}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≳λk+2​M≳(k∨M)−a.\displaystyle\gtrsim\lambda_{k+2M}\gtrsim(k\vee M)^{-{a}}.

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M).1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Therefore

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)≲1\displaystyle\frac{\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}{\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}\lesssim 1

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} when k/M≲1k/M\lesssim 1.

On the other hand, when kk is relatively large, using Lemma G.1 with 𝐇k:∞\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty} replacing 𝐇\mathbf{H} again, we obtain

≥c2​[(M+k)−a+(k0+k)1−aM]−c3⋅(k0+1+k)−a\displaystyle\geq c_{2}\Big[\big({M}+k\big)^{-{a}}+\frac{(k_{0}+k)^{1-{a}}}{M}\Big]-c_{3}\cdot(k_{0}+1+k)^{-{a}}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)−e−Ω⁡(k0)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}-e^{-\Omega(k_{0})}, where c1,c2,c3>0c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}>0 are some universal constants. Choosing k0=M/c2k_{0}=M/c^{2} for some sufficiently large constant c>0c>0, we further obtain

μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≥c4​(M+k)−a​[1+kM]−c5​(M+k)−a\displaystyle\geq c_{4}\big({M}+k\big)^{-{a}}\Big[1+\frac{k}{M}\Big]-c_{5}(M+k)^{-{a}}
≥c6​(M∨k)−a​[1∨kM]−c7​(M∨k)−a\displaystyle\geq c_{6}\big({M}\vee k\big)^{-{a}}\Big[1\vee\frac{k}{M}\Big]-c_{7}(M\vee k)^{-{a}} (36)

c6​(M∨k)−a​[1∨kM]−c7​(M∨k)−a≥c62​(k∨M)−a​(1∨kM)\displaystyle c_{6}\big({M}\vee k\big)^{-{a}}\Big[1\vee\frac{k}{M}\Big]-c_{7}(M\vee k)^{-{a}}\geq\frac{c_{6}}{2}(k\vee M)^{-{a}}\big(1\vee\frac{k}{M}\big)

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. ∎

G.3 Concentration results under logarithmic power-law spectrum

Lemma G.6 (Theorem 6 in (Bartlett et al., 2020)).

Suppose Assumption 4 hold. Then there exist some aa-dependent constants c,c~>0c,\tilde{c}>0 such that, with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}

μj​(𝐒𝐇𝐒⊤)∈{[c⋅j−1​log−a⁡(j+1),c~⋅j−1​log−a⁡(j+1)]j≤𝗄∗,[c⋅M−1​log1−a⁡(M),c~⋅M−1​log1−a⁡(M)]𝗄∗<j≤M,\displaystyle\mu_{j}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{S}^{\top})\in\begin{cases}[c\cdot j^{-1}\log^{-a}(j+1),\tilde{c}\cdot j^{-1}\log^{-a}(j+1)]&j\leq{\mathsf{k^{*}}},\\ [c\cdot M^{-1}\log^{1-a}(M),\tilde{c}\cdot M^{-1}\log^{1-a}(M)]&{\mathsf{k^{*}}}<j\leq M,\end{cases}

where 𝗄∗≂M/log⁡(M){\mathsf{k^{*}}}\eqsim M/\log(M). Also, there exists some aa-dependent constants c1,c2>0c_{1},c_{2}>0 such that

c1j​log2​a​(j+1)≤μj​(𝐒𝐇2​𝐒⊤)≤c2j​log2​a​(j+1)\displaystyle\frac{c_{1}}{j\log^{2a}(j+1)}\leq\mu_{j}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}^{2}\mathbf{S}^{\top})\leq\frac{c_{2}}{j\log^{2a}(j+1)}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

The proof is adapted from the proof of Theorem 6 in (Bartlett et al., 2020). We include it here for completeness.

First part of Lemma G.6.

In Lemma G.1, for some constant c>1c>1, choose

𝗄∗:=min⁡{k≥0:∑i>kλi≥c⋅M⋅λk+1}.{\mathsf{k^{*}}}:=\min\bigg\{k\geq 0:\sum_{i>k}\lambda_{i}\geq c\cdot M\cdot\lambda_{k+1}\bigg\}.

where c1>1c_{1}>1 is a constant.

Therefore, we have

λ~j\displaystyle\tilde{\lambda}_{j} ≂λj+∑i>𝗄∗λiM\displaystyle\eqsim\lambda_{j}+\frac{\sum_{i>{\mathsf{k^{*}}}}\lambda_{i}}{M}
≂{j−1​log−a⁡(j+1)j≤𝗄∗,M−1​log1−a⁡(M)𝗄∗<j≤M,\displaystyle\eqsim\begin{cases}j^{-1}\log^{-a}(j+1)&j\leq{\mathsf{k^{*}}},\\ M^{-1}\log^{1-a}(M)&{\mathsf{k^{*}}}<j\leq M,\end{cases}

where 𝗄∗≂M/log⁡(M){\mathsf{k^{*}}}\eqsim M/\log(M).

Let λ¯i\bar{\lambda}_{i} denote the ii-th eigenvalue of 𝐒𝐇2​𝐒⊤\mathbf{S}\mathbf{H}^{2}\mathbf{S}^{\top} for i∈[M]i\in[M]. 12⋅j−2​log−2​a⁡(j+1)−c~2⋅M−2​log−2​a​M\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\cdot j^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}(j+1)-\tilde{c}_{2}\cdot M^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}M
≤λ¯j≤32⋅(j−2​log−2​a⁡(j+1)+c~1​M−2​log−2​a​M)+c~2⋅M−2​log−2​a​M\displaystyle\qquad\leq\bar{\lambda}_{j}\leq\frac{3}{2}\cdot(j^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}(j+1)+\tilde{c}_{1}M^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}M)+\tilde{c}_{2}\cdot M^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}M

for every j∈[M]j\in[M] for some constants c~i,i∈[2]\tilde{c}_{i},i\in[2] with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Therefore, for all j≤M/c~j\leq M/\tilde{c} for some sufficiently large constant c~>1\tilde{c}>1, we have

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constants c~3,c~4>0\tilde{c}_{3},\tilde{c}_{4}>0. For j∈[M/c~,M]j\in[M/\tilde{c},M], by monotonicity of the eigenvalues, we have

for some constants c5,c6>0c_{5},c_{6}>0 with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Moreover, using Lemma G.2 with k=0k=0, we obtain

λ¯j≥λ¯M≥μmin(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞2𝐒k:∞⊤)≥c~7λ¯2​M≥c~8⋅j−2log−2​a(j+1)\displaystyle\bar{\lambda}_{j}\geq\bar{\lambda}_{M}\geq{\mu_{\min}}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}^{2}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top})\geq\tilde{c}_{7}\bar{\lambda}_{2M}\geq\tilde{c}_{8}\cdot j^{-2}\log^{-2{a}}(j+1)

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constants c~7,c~8>0\tilde{c}_{7},\tilde{c}_{8}>0 when j∈[M/c~,M]j\in[M/\tilde{c},M]. Combining the bounds for j≤M/c~j\leq M/\tilde{c} and j∈[M/c~,M]j\in[M/\tilde{c},M] completes the proof. ∎

Lemma G.7 (Ratio of eigenvalues of 𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}_{k:\infty}^{\top} under logarithmic power-law spectrum).

Suppose Assumption 4 hold. There exists some aa-dependent constant c>0c>0 such that for any k≥1k\geq 1, the ratio between the M/2M/2-th and MM-th eigenvalues

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)≤c\displaystyle\frac{\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}{\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}\leq c

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M).1-e^{-\Omega(M)}.

Proof of Lemma G.7.

Similar to the proof of Lemma G.5, we prove the lemma under two scenarios where kk is relatively small (or large) compared with MM.

Let c>0c>0 be some sufficiently large constant. Applying Lemma G.1 with 𝐇k:∞\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty} replacing 𝐇\mathbf{H}, for k0=M/ck_{0}=M/c, we have

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≤32⋅(λM/2+k+∑i>k0λi+kM)+c1⋅λk0+1+k,\displaystyle\leq\frac{3}{2}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{M/2+k}+\frac{\sum_{i>k_{0}}\lambda_{i+k}}{M}\bigg)+c_{1}\cdot\lambda_{k_{0}+1+k},
≲(M2+k)−1​log−a⁡(M2+k)+log1−a⁡(k0+k)M+log−a⁡(k0+1+k)k0+1+k\displaystyle\lesssim\big(\frac{M}{2}+k\big)^{-1}\log^{-a}\big(\frac{M}{2}+k\big)+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(k_{0}+k)}{M}+\frac{\log^{-{a}}(k_{0}+1+k)}{k_{0}+1+k}
≲log−a⁡(M+k)(M+k)+log1−a⁡(M+k)M≲log1−a⁡(M+k)M\displaystyle\lesssim\frac{\log^{-a}(M+k)}{(M+k)}+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}\lesssim\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M} (37)

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} for some constant c1>0c_{1}>0.

Case 11: k≲Mk\lesssim M.

Applying Lemma G.1 with 𝐇k:∞\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty} replacing 𝐇\mathbf{H}, for k0=M/ck_{0}=M/c, we have

μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≳12⋅(λM+k+∑i>k0λi+kM)−c1⋅λk0+1+k,\displaystyle\gtrsim\frac{1}{2}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{M+k}+\frac{\sum_{i>k_{0}}\lambda_{i+k}}{M}\bigg)-c_{1}\cdot\lambda_{k_{0}+1+k},
≳(M+k)−1​log−a⁡(M+k)+log1−a⁡(k0+k)M−c​log−a⁡(k0+1+k)k0+1+k\displaystyle\gtrsim\big({M}+k\big)^{-1}\log^{-a}\big({M}+k\big)+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(k_{0}+k)}{M}-c\frac{\log^{-{a}}(k_{0}+1+k)}{k_{0}+1+k}
≳log−a⁡(M+k)(M+k)+log1−a⁡(M+k)M−c~​log−a⁡(M)M\displaystyle\gtrsim\frac{\log^{-a}(M+k)}{(M+k)}+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}-\tilde{c}\frac{\log^{-{a}}(M)}{M}
≳log1−a⁡MM\displaystyle\gtrsim\frac{\log^{1-{a}}M}{M}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}. Therefore,

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)≲[log1−a⁡(M+k)M]/[log1−a⁡MM]≲1\displaystyle\frac{\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}{\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}\lesssim\Big[\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}\Big]\Big/\Big[\frac{\log^{1-{a}}M}{M}\Big]\lesssim 1

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} when k/M≲1k/M\lesssim 1.

Case 22: k≳Mk\gtrsim M.

On the other hand, when kk is relatively large, using Lemma G.1 with 𝐇k:∞\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty} replacing 𝐇\mathbf{H} and k0=M/ck_{0}=M/c again, we obtain

μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒k:∞⊤)\displaystyle\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty}) ≥12⋅(λM+k+∑i>k0λi+kM)−c1⋅λk0+1+k,\displaystyle\geq\frac{1}{2}\cdot\bigg(\lambda_{M+k}+\frac{\sum_{i>k_{0}}\lambda_{i+k}}{M}\bigg)-c_{1}\cdot\lambda_{k_{0}+1+k},
≳(M+k)−1​log−a⁡(M+k)+log1−a⁡(k0+k)M−c2​log−a⁡(k0+1+k)k0+1+k\displaystyle\gtrsim\big({M}+k\big)^{-1}\log^{-a}\big({M}+k\big)+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(k_{0}+k)}{M}-c_{2}\frac{\log^{-{a}}(k_{0}+1+k)}{k_{0}+1+k}
≳k−1​log−a⁡(k)+log1−a⁡(M+k)M−c3​log−a⁡(M+k)M+k\displaystyle\gtrsim k^{-1}\log^{-a}\big(k\big)+\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}-c_{3}\frac{\log^{-{a}}(M+k)}{M+k}
≳log1−a⁡(M+k)M\displaystyle\gtrsim\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)}, where c1,c2,c3>0c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}>0 are some aa-dependent constants. Therefore,

μM/2(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)μM(𝐒k:∞𝐇k:∞𝐒⊤k:∞)≲[log1−a⁡(M+k)M]/[log1−a⁡(M+k)M]≲1\displaystyle\frac{\mu_{M/2}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}{\mu_{M}(\mathbf{S}_{{k:\infty}}\mathbf{H}_{k:\infty}\mathbf{S}^{\top}_{k:\infty})}\lesssim\Big[\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}\Big]\Big/\Big[\frac{\log^{1-{a}}(M+k)}{M}\Big]\lesssim 1

with probability at least 1−e−Ω⁡(M)1-e^{-\Omega(M)} when k/M≳1k/M\gtrsim 1. ∎
